status: All eight initial scanner-workflow decisions resolved. Sixteen subsequent implementation choices are agreed, including the compact PMR report/reference interface and unchanged MacRoman table dependency approved 28 October. The internal PMR expected-failure route remains under clarification. The independent shared ID helper and its focused test/library are implemented and verified; PMR/source readers and scanner remain pending. New concrete choices still require check-ins. No app cutover or measured scan improvement.

instruction.quote: Can you make a point, to check-in with ME at every decision. Give me a list of the decisions explained in plain English and the recommendation highlighted. Do not always assume, do not hallucinate - ground yourself in the plan and the codebase every now and then.

workingAgreement: Check in at every new decision, including internal engineering choices.
Explain options in plain English, highlight the recommendation, give its reason/tradeoff and relevant plan/code evidence.
Separate approved decisions, observed current behavior, proposals and unknowns.
Normally one decision at a time; await the answer before dependent implementation.
Keep approved metadata/result/Cancel rules; revisit only with a stated new reason.
Read-only evidence gathering may continue while an answer is pending.
Record each answer before building on it. Recheck current source revision periodically and before relying on implementation claims.
Do not claim speed/memory improvements without measurements. Bring later concrete choices back instead of assuming a broad policy approves every number, label or layout.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer to the asynchronous build-boundary question
implementationDecisions.question: How should Bella be compiled during development?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: A separate mediamuster_bella static library, using Qt Core and initially linked only to Bella's focused tests, in the existing CMake build.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Compile Bella sources directly into test programs and introduce a library later.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Use the separate static library with the existing C++17 and exact Qt 6.5.3 settings. Keep the app using OldScanner and leave Bin Filter unchanged.
implementationDecisions.scope: Build boundary only. Source/header layout, parser signatures and result structures require subsequent check-ins before dependent code. No progress, MediaFile/table, journal, Unfinished Business, Undo or Bin Filter integration is approved by this answer.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Implemented: mediamuster_bella contains the independent shared ID helper, linked only to its focused tests and Qt Core.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer after explanation and comparison with 86c500ca6bf9cc93529017979d0f1b3ddac856be
implementationDecisions.question: Should the PMR parser receive captured bytes, or read the file itself?
options: Option 1: caller captures the PMR bytes, parser interprets them.
Option 2: PMR parser accepts a file path and handles both reading and interpretation.
implementationDecisions.answer: Lets go with Option 2 - the PMR parser does both jobs.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Provide a path-based PMR parser entry point that reads the source once into scoped memory and returns compact owned results after interpreting it. The caller need not acquire the bytes first.
implementationDecisions.recommendationHistory: Initially recommended caller capture for reuse and direct tests. Historical source comparison showed 86c500c already used scoped whole-file capture plus small memory-decoding helpers. Neither API boundary has a demonstrated simplicity or runtime advantage. A thin-wrapper arrangement was subsequently proposed; the user explicitly selected Option 2.
implementationDecisions.scope: PMR acquisition boundary only. Small internal helpers are possible, but no separate public byte-parser interface, shared capture layer or thin wrapper is required by this choice. Other parser acquisition APIs are not settled here. Preserve approved cancellation, changed-source handling, lifetimes, complete identities, whole-set rejection/fallback and text rules; do not adopt historical DTM, recovery or other differing behavior.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; the shared ID helper is implemented independently. PMR signatures, result details and capture/check mechanisms remain pending.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer after a plain-English report analogy
implementationDecisions.question: Should the PMR parser return one report containing its entries, outcome and explanation, or return these through separate outputs?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: One owned returned result containing entries, outcome and explanatory/diagnostic details together.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Return entries and provide status/details through separate output parameters, expanding 86c500c's yes/no flag to preserve Bella's required distinctions.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Return the PMR entries, outcome and explanation together in one owned result. Preserve approved distinctions between usable metadata and unavailable, failed, changed or cancelled reads.
implementationDecisions.scope: Returned-result shape only. Does not settle exact type/field names, outcome/detail representation, cancellation input, source stamps or capture/change-check mechanisms. Path-based acquisition remains agreed. No new visible feature or performance claim.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; the PMR report is not implemented yet. The shared ID helper/library is a separate completed increment.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer to the reader/report placement question
implementationDecisions.question: Should each reader's entry/report definitions live beside that reader, or in an additional shared types.h?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: Keep each reader's report beside that reader, with the already-agreed shared ID helper separate.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Introduce a shared types.h containing the report definitions for all formats.
implementationDecisions.answer: Lets go with the recommended arrangement, keeping each reader's report beside its reader.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Put shared identity types/functions in mobid.h/.cpp and PMR entry/report definitions beside its reader in pmrparser.h/.cpp. Add their focused tests through explicit existing root/test CMake lists. Do not introduce a common types.h now.
implementationDecisions.scope: Initial filenames and placement only. Does not settle exact interfaces or stored representations, cancellation or source-change mechanisms. No app integration, cutover or performance claim.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: mobid.h/.cpp, tst_bellamobid.cpp and their library/test entries are implemented. PMR files remain pending; no parser placeholders were added.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer, item 1 of the three ID-helper choices
implementationDecisions.question: Should Bella use the existing database or MXF convention for its normalized internal ID numeric fields?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: Existing database convention: little-endian spelling of numeric fields on every host, preserving all other ID bytes.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Use MXF's big-endian spelling internally, with explicit conversion from other sources.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Use the database convention under the concrete first ID-helper contract in Project Bella/README.md. Continue to interpret each input using its explicitly supplied layout and declared byte order.
implementationDecisions.scope: Internal canonical spelling, not changed source interpretation or displayed-ID formatting. No runtime performance advantage is established.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer, item 2 of the three ID-helper choices
implementationDecisions.question: Should Bella use one labelled fixed-size ID container or separate modern and older ID types in a common holder?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: One private 32-byte std::array plus a form label; modern/recognized IDs have 32 active bytes and unfamiliar legacy UIDs have 12 active bytes. Unused storage is not part of the ID.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Separate 32-byte and 12-byte types inside an inline variant, which still reserves room for its largest alternative.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Use the single labelled owned container, with read-only kind/active-byte access, full active-byte equality and QHash support, as described in the concrete first ID-helper contract.
implementationDecisions.scope: Storage and interface of the shared ID helper only. Preserve the complete unfamiliar legacy UID and distinguish its form. No automatic memory saving is claimed; the earlier variant-space explanation was corrected before the answer.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer, item 3 of the three ID-helper choices
implementationDecisions.question: Should incomplete ID bytes return an ordinary failure answer or raise a typed conversion exception?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: Return either the complete owned ID or a named InvalidWidth result; the caller checks it and provides source/field context in the PMR report.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Raise a typed conversion exception which the reader catches and converts to its report.
implementationDecisions.answer: Recommended: expected bad input follows the ordinary reply route. The caller must check the answer.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Use MobIdResult, a std::variant<MobId, MobIdError>, returned by normalizeMobId(QByteArrayView, MobIdLayout, ByteOrder), under the concrete first ID-helper contract. Wrong byte counts return MobIdError::InvalidWidth normally.
implementationDecisions.scope: The bounded shared ID conversion, not PMR capture/cancel/change-check mechanisms or a blanket exception policy. This approval enables mobid.h/.cpp, its focused test and the existing-CMake static-library wiring; no PMR stubs or app integration.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human choice of shared stop flag, followed by a question about its use across readers/parsers
implementationDecisions.question: How should the PMR reader notice Cancel: a shared stop flag or a function it calls to ask whether to stop?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: One shared thread-safe stop flag observed by the reader between reading and decoding steps.
implementationDecisions.alternative: A function the reader calls for customised stop checks, adding another callable interface.
implementationDecisions.answer: Lets go with the shared stop flag. Would all readers/parsers use this same stop flag?
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Use the same per-scan stop request for the Bella organiser and every PMR/MDB/MXF/OMF/native WAVE/AIFF source job. Cancel stops new work and requests cooperative stopping of active readers. Each later scan gets fresh uncancelled state only after prior cleanup.
implementationDecisions.clarification: Same flag means within one Bella scan. It is not global across scans and is not shared with Bin Filter or file operations. Small bounded helpers such as the ID normalizer need no flag parameter; the reader checks between units of work. Blocking OS reads may delay stopping.
implementationDecisions.scope: Shared cancellation signal and per-scan scope. Exact parser parameter types, checkpoint placement, lifetime/wakeup, source-change and publication mechanisms still need concrete check-ins. Preserve responsive cleanup and partial results; do not copy the existing blocking GUI shutdown path or change active OldScanner/Bin Filter/file operations.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; no cancellation runtime code added yet.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer to the PMR reading/checkpoint choice
implementationDecisions.question: Should Bella capture a PMR in up-to-1-MiB pieces with stop checks between requests, or request the whole file in one call with checks before and after?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOptionAtQuestion: A small up-to-1-MiB read loop, giving additional opportunities to observe cancellation during large captures.
implementationDecisions.selectedAlternative: Single whole-file call, as in 86c500c, with Cancel checks before and after the call.
implementationDecisions.answer: Go with Alternative: request the whole file in one call, as 86c500c did. Bella would check Cancel before and after that call. Pro: less reading code.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Use QFile::readAll() for the PMR capture and check the shared scan stop flag before and after it. Do not introduce the proposed 1-MiB capture loop or intermediate capture checkpoints.
implementationDecisions.tradeoff: Fewer reading-code steps; Bella cannot inspect its stop flag while readAll is running. A blocked OS read can delay return. Both options retain one full PMR capture, so this establishes neither a memory cap nor a performance advantage.
implementationDecisions.scope: PMR capture request and its before/after cancellation checks only. Does not choose parse-loop checkpoints, exact report/API representation, source-change detection or capture-error precedence. Path-based parser ownership, read-once extraction/release and all existing PMR format rules remain.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; PMR runtime code remains pending.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer to the PMR change-detection facts question
implementationDecisions.question: Should Bella check disk-file identity plus size/modification time before and after reading, or use simpler Qt-only size/modification-time checks?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOptionAtQuestion: Disk-file identity plus size and modification time, including checking that the path still identifies the opened file.
implementationDecisions.selectedAlternative: Size and modification time only, using Qt-only code.
implementationDecisions.answer: If databases are updated, they always have the same msmFMID.pmr etc name. Check only the size and modification time with simpler Qt-only code.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Compare PMR size and modification time before and after its one QFile::readAll capture. Use Qt-only checks and do not add native disk identity or path-to-open-handle identity checks.
implementationDecisions.tradeoff: Fewer platform-specific mechanisms. A same-size, same-time replacement or rewrite may escape detection. The standard database name does not itself prove unchanged file identity or contents.
implementationDecisions.scope: PMR change-check facts only. Report/exclude detected changed reads and leave a fresh attempt to manual rescan, as already agreed. Exact stamp/report representation and unavailable-check handling remain pending. Do not link or modify file-operation code for this check.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; PMR runtime code remains pending.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer selecting the alternative in-memory parsing checkpoint policy
implementationDecisions.question: After the whole PMR is in memory, should its parser check Cancel before each record or before and after a complete record set?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOptionAtQuestion: Before each record, including during base framing and selected/fallback decoding.
implementationDecisions.selectedAlternative: Before and after a complete record set.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Check the shared stop flag before and after each complete record-set pass, covering safe base-set framing/traversal and selected/fallback set decoding. Do not add per-record polling or a periodic record counter.
implementationDecisions.tradeoff: Fewer stop checks; a Cancel request during a set waits for its next set boundary. No speed or stopping-latency advantage has been measured.
implementationDecisions.scope: In-memory PMR parsing checkpoint granularity. Whole-file readAll and its before/after checks remain unchanged. Whole-set validation, no entry salvage and all existing source/partial-scan rules remain. Exact report/API and capture-check failure details still need their concrete review.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; PMR runtime code remains pending.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human answer to the readable-PMR/unavailable-check policy question
implementationDecisions.question: If Bella reads a PMR but cannot obtain the size/date information required to verify it, should its metadata be unused or retained with unverified status?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOptionAtQuestion: Return could-not-verify and leave that PMR's metadata unused.
implementationDecisions.selectedAlternative: Keep otherwise valid PMR metadata and mark it unverified.
implementationDecisions.answer: I think we should keep the PMR metadata and mark it unverified.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Retain an otherwise valid captured/whole-set PMR contribution when the required size/modification-time check cannot be completed. Mark it unverified and preserve the reason; carry that qualification through later matching/status handling.
implementationDecisions.scope: Unavailable verification facts, not an observed change or failed capture/format. A detected change still excludes that read. Invalid sets remain invalid, and no automatic retry, stronger native identity check or changed source-opening rule is introduced.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; the PMR report and parser remain pending.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human confirmation after comparing exact 86c500c parser and scanner behavior
implementationDecisions.question: Should Bella use a complete known set's metadata despite an unknown extension or trailing content, or withhold that PMR's metadata as 86c500c did?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOptionAtConfirmation: Match 86c500c for unknown-extra-content PMR metadata eligibility.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Keep one complete known set's metadata with a distinct unknown-extra-content qualification, without interpreting or searching those unknown bytes.
implementationDecisions.answer: Yes, let's match the behaviour of 86c500c for unknown extensions or trailing content. Record that decision.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Unknown extension versions after the base set, or unexplained content after the declared v16 set, make that PMR unsupported and its metadata unavailable. Do not use an otherwise complete known set's metadata in this case.
implementationDecisions.historicalBehavior: At 86c500c, unknown extensions and trailing v16 content return older entries with ok=false. The scanner merges only ok=true indexes, so those returned entries never become selected PMR metadata. The v16 set is not promoted before the trailing-content check.
implementationDecisions.scope: This unknown-content metadata-eligibility case only; implement independently. Supported versions, whole-set selection/rejection and safely located fallback for damaged supported sets remain agreed. Physical inventory/reference-check meanings and keeping otherwise valid size/date-unverified metadata remain unchanged. No unknown-format interpretation, raw search, retry, existing scanner modification or cutover.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; PMR runtime code remains pending.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human selection of two separate answers inside the single PMR report
implementationDecisions.question: Should the one report describe reading result and size/date verification separately, or use one combined label for every pairing?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: Separate reading/parsing result and size/date verification answers within the same owned report.
implementationDecisions.alternative: One combined status label for every completion/verification pairing.
implementationDecisions.answer: two separate answers inside the same report. E.g. For a readable PMR whose modification date was unavailable: Reading result: Completed; Size/date check: Unverified; Metadata: Retained
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Represent the reading/parsing outcome and capture-verification qualification as separate fields in the same PMR report. Valid metadata can be retained with Completed + Unverified, as already approved.
implementationDecisions.scope: Report representation only. No new UI column, scanning behavior or source rule. Exact names and the remaining compact report/API contract will be reviewed together, rather than through isolated naming decisions.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; PMR runtime code remains pending.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human selection of recommended item 1 in the consolidated PMR proposal
implementationDecisions.question: Should the report keep one complete known record set with explicit use/coverage qualifications, or separate metadata and reference record lists?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: The concrete parsePmr(path, const atomic stop flag reference) interface and compact report in Project Bella/README.md, with one whole known set, independent read/check results, partial available stamp facts, metadata eligibility and format-level reference coverage.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Separate metadata and reference record lists inside the same report, with their own bookkeeping.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Use the consolidated contract's names, types, retained values and reference qualifications. Keep only whole validated sets; unsupported extra content never supplies metadata. Any retained whole-set reference-only facts remain subject to the existing scanner's name/ID/source qualification and cannot establish unsupported negative coverage. Valid empty-set coverage is distinct from missing or damaged data.
implementationDecisions.scope: Concrete PMR interface/report/reference representation, including its pure stamp-comparison helper and settled input/format/cancellation semantics. No new per-entry histories, graphs, source opens, flag wrapper, native identity check, display column, NoReference rule or app integration. The internal expected-failure mechanism is explicitly not approved by item 1.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; PMR runtime code waits on clarification of the remaining expected-failure route.

implementationDecisions.source: Direct human selection of recommended item 3 in the consolidated PMR proposal
implementationDecisions.question: Should the new fixed-MacRoman Bella decoder reuse the existing immutable character table or keep a separate mapping inside Bella?
implementationDecisions.recommendedOption: Reuse only AvidText::kMacRomanHigh[128] in unchanged src/avidtext.h with fresh unconditional MacRoman decoding logic in Bella.
implementationDecisions.alternative: Duplicate the same fixed mapping inside Bella to remove the shared-header dependency.
implementationDecisions.agreedRule: Allow this generic existing-header dependency without editing the header or linking OldScanner. Never call AvidText::decode for Bella PMR fields because it tries UTF-8 first. Keep fixed MacRoman for Project/legacy Filename and strict UTF-8 for v16 Filename.
implementationDecisions.scope: Immutable character-mapping data only. No existing reader/decoder implementation is adopted or changed; Bin Filter and the active scanner remain unchanged. No measured performance claim.
implementationDecisions.implementationStatus: Recorded; the dependency will be added with the independent PMR parser.

agreedEngineeringDecisions.title: How many reads at once?
agreedEngineeringDecisions.recommendation: Four reads total shared by PMR/MDB/required headers.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.alternative: Up to four PMRs plus four MDBs together; header allowance decided separately.

approval.source: Direct human answer to asynchronous decision 1
approval.question: First decision: should Bella share four reading jobs between PMR, MDB and required media headers, or allow four PMRs plus four MDBs at once? I recommend four total initially to limit competing reads and temporary memory; its speed still needs measuring. If you choose four of each, we would decide the header limit separately.
approval.agreedRule: Maximum four source-reading jobs total across PMR, MDB and required media headers.
approval.scope: Approves the combined source-job ceiling only. Worker organisation, memory admission, lifecycle and other pending choices remain unapproved.

agreedEngineeringDecisions.title: Who organises the work?
agreedEngineeringDecisions.recommendation: One background organiser and one reusable shared worker group.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.alternative: Separate worker groups by format, with no more than four source-reading jobs total across them.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.condition: Background organiser separate from four source-reader slots; one shared team chosen. Detailed handoff/lifetime/memory policies remain separate decisions.

approval.source: Direct human answer to asynchronous decision 2
approval.question: Decision 2: how should Bella organise those four reading jobs? I recommend one background organiser with one shared team of readers: the organiser assigns work and collects results, while the readers handle PMR, MDB or headers. The alternative is separate teams for each format. Both options stay within four reading jobs total; the organiser is separate from those readers. A shared team gives us one place to manage the limit and fewer queues. OldScanner already has one background organiser, but reads databases sequentially.
approval.agreedRule: One background organiser and one reusable shared reader team, with at most four source-reading jobs total across PMR/MDB/required headers; organiser outside reader slots.
approval.scope: Approves work organisation. Does not approve pending compact-lookup lifetime, memory admission, capture/retry, cleanup, progress or Duration sorting policies.

agreedEngineeringDecisions.title: When to release extracted database information?
agreedEngineeringDecisions.recommendation: Keep required compact source-qualified file/master facts until all file/header matches and dependent checks finish, then release them.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.alternative: Investigate earlier release with explicit dependency management, preserving every eligible cross-folder match.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.condition: Release raw database buffers and parser workspace after extraction as already agreed. Do not discard compact metadata merely because its source folder is finished; do not arbitrarily keep one record per full ID when sources disagree.

approval.source: Direct human instruction following the ELI5 clarification
approval.statement: OK understood. Let's lock that in for Bella: keep the useful notes until all files have been matched, then release them. does the app currently work like that? What's the next decision?
approval.agreedRule: Keep required compact matching information available until all files have been matched, then release the temporary catalogue. Full database buffers and parser workspace still release after extraction.
approval.scope: Approves compact-lookup lifetime. Does not change matching-source eligibility, retain permanent parser graphs/cache, discard required final row/status/operation facts, or approve memory-based scheduling.
approval.clarificationBeforeApproval: The earlier reply asking for ELI5 was not approval; the explicit lock-in followed the book/notes explanation.

agreedEngineeringDecisions.title: What if databases are large?
agreedEngineeringDecisions.recommendation: Measure and report actual findings without added RAM caps or automatic memory controls; preserve the separately agreed four-job maximum.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.alternative: Add automatic memory-based admission now; estimates and numerical thresholds still need concrete evidence and a further user decision.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.condition: No RAM quota, arbitrary database-size policy limit or automatic memory-based reader reduction. Existing type/bounds/extent checks remain; four jobs are not a fixed byte limit. Findings do not authorise a later control.

approval.source: Direct human answer to asynchronous decision4
approval.question: Decision 4: should Bella automatically use fewer readers when databases are large? I recommend testing the agreed four-reader design and measuring its memory use first, then bringing you any demonstrated need for extra controls. The alternative is to add automatic memory controls now, with their memory threshold still to be decided. Both options keep the four-job maximum. Four jobs are not a fixed memory limit, and Bella's actual peak memory use is not measured yet.
approval.answer: Lets measure- but no caps or memory controls. Lets just see the findings
approval.agreedRule: Measure the agreed design and present findings; do not add RAM caps or automatic memory controls.
approval.scope: Memory-policy decision only. The existing four-source-job maximum is preserved because the question explicitly retains it in both options; no new approval is implied for later memory controls. Existing parser safety/extent validation remains.
approval.measurementTiming: Bella runtime is not implemented yet. Actual Bella measurements follow an executable independent implementation; no findings fabricated from source review.

agreedEngineeringDecisions.title: What if a file changes during reading?
agreedEngineeringDecisions.recommendation: Exclude the changed read, report it and allow manual rescan. Keep the physical row and independently valid information; apply only already-approved fallback rules.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.alternative: Add one fresh retry of the changed source, with recapture/identity safety explicitly defined.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.condition: An unusable database may permit the agreed header fallback. Changed physical media invalidates facts tied to its earlier identity. Current OldScanner does not reread changed PMR/MDB sources; a fresh retry would be new. Exact change checks are distinct from the ignored PMR DTM.

approval.source: Direct human answer to asynchronous decision5
approval.question: Decision 5: if a database or media file changes while Bella is reading it, what should happen? I recommend ignoring that changed read, reporting the change and letting you rescan. The physical file stays listed, and unaffected valid information and our agreed fallbacks can still be used. Alternative: automatically try reading the changed source once more. That might recover a finished update, but adds work and may find another change. OldScanner already excludes changed database data without rereading it.
approval.agreedRule: Exclude and report a detected changed read; leave a fresh recapture to manual rescan. Retain the physical row and independently valid facts; apply only previously approved fallback rules.
approval.scope: No automatic fresh source retry or new blank-field header trigger. Does not use ignored PMR DTM or change approved same-buffer PMR set fallback. Facts tied to replaced media's earlier identity are not unaffected valid information. Detailed change-check mechanism remains to be specified.

agreedEngineeringDecisions.title: How to wait for Cancel or closing?
agreedEngineeringDecisions.recommendation: Preserve current responsive Cancel and keep the interface responsive while shared readers stop and cleanup finishes; allow another scan/final app close only after safe cleanup.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.alternative: Retain synchronous restart/shutdown waiting on the calling thread, as used by the current BackgroundJob.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.condition: Current Cancel is already nonblocking and shows Cancelling. The proposed change extends responsiveness through pool cleanup and app closing; it does not change agreed partial-result retention. Blocked OS/network reads can delay safe completion with either approach.

approval.source: Direct human answer to asynchronous decision6
approval.question: Decision 6: how should Bella finish stopping its readers when you cancel or quit during a scan? I recommend keeping the window responsive while the readers stop safely and release their working data. Another scan or final app close would wait until that cleanup finishes; partial results stay as agreed. The alternative is to reuse the current restart/shutdown waiting method, which can pause the calling interface. Current Cancel already responds immediately and shows “Cancelling…”; the shutdown/cleanup path is the proposed change. A blocked drive read could still delay finishing.
approval.agreedRule: Preserve responsive Cancel and keep the window responsive while readers stop safely and release working data. Permit another scan or final app close only after cleanup; partial results remain as agreed.
approval.scope: High-level Bella scan cleanup/closing behaviour. Does not approve every detailed state/API/lifetime mechanism automatically, force thread termination, add overlapping scans, or guarantee an instant finish for blocked OS reads. File-operation engine/Bin Filter scope remains unchanged.

approval.source: Direct human answer to asynchronous decision7
approval.question: Decision 7: how often should the progress display refresh? I recommend showing the latest count and file path about five times per second, while scanning continues normally. Stage changes, Cancel, errors and finishing would still be shown promptly. Keep the current warning details, file paths and diagnostic logging/batching. The alternative is to keep the current per-file progress updates. I checked the code: warnings are already batched, so I’m not proposing warning suppression or summaries.

agreedEngineeringDecisions.title: How should Duration sort?
agreedEngineeringDecisions.recommendation: Chosen policy: preserve current numeric displayed HH/MM/SS/FF order and Kind ties for equal displayed tuples.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.alternative: Preserve comparison of numeric displayed HH/MM/SS/FF components, with current Kind tie order.
agreedEngineeringDecisions.condition: Sorting only; no extra reads or new Duration display/export convention. Preserve blank grouping and existing equivalent-row behaviour. Earlier Bella known-zero/rounded-zero display rules still apply.

rejectedProposal.recommendationAtQuestion: Sort available Duration values by exact elapsed duration. Keep approved timecode display/CSV, current unavailable grouping and Kind tie order.

approval.source: Direct human answer to asynchronous decision8
approval.question: Decision 8: should Duration sort by actual running time, shortest first, or by the displayed timecode numbers as today? I recommend actual running time when frame rates differ. Illustrative example: 20 frames at 25 fps lasts 0.8 seconds; 24 frames at 60 fps lasts 0.4 seconds. Current timecode sorting puts 20 before 24; actual-time sorting puts the shorter file first, so the displayed numbers can look out of order. The timecode display and CSV stay unchanged, with existing blank grouping and equal-duration tie handling.
approval.agreedRule: Compare numeric displayed(HH,MM,SS,FF) tuples. Equal displayed tuples use Audio/Video/Unknown and existing equivalent-row behaviour. Keep unavailable grouping first ascending; descending reverses order. No elapsed-time key or lexical string comparison.
approval.scope: User chose the alternative, not the elapsed-time recommendation. Exact Length/rate interpretation and Duration maths remain required for display. Preserve earlier known-zero/rounded-zero corrections. Duration display/export convention is unchanged by sorting; earlier Bella field exclusions/renames remain. No new source reads or filename tiebreak.

currentLifetimeCheck.head: c2cc89e9404fae5f84787c624f14e16d862d68bc
currentLifetimeCheck.answer: Yes, broadly. Current OldScanner releases each full database capture/parsed objects after projection, retains extracted facts/global indexes through matching, then releases the working session after formatting final rows.
currentLifetimeCheck.difference: OldScanner projections retain richer observations including raw field values, source references and explanations. Bella plans fewer required facts and simpler representation. Final rows already avoid owning the scan session; required status/operation receipts remain.

codeAnchors.finding: Scoped image/parsed objects; returns projection plus SourceReceipt.
ScanResult session lives through final row preparation; scoped release on return.
Final rows receive values/status/operation checks, not working scan owners.

currentLifetimeCheck.measurement: Source-only check; no runtime or memory measurements. No claim that this lifetime pattern itself is new or proves a saving.

measurementDirective.answer: Lets measure- but no caps or memory controls. Lets just see the findings

currentChangedSourceCheck.head: c2cc89e9404fae5f84787c624f14e16d862d68bc
findings: Current coordinator excludes facts from a source detected missing or modified after discovery.
Each PMR/MDB is prepared once; changed databases are not reread.
A bounded later pass reconsiders unopened headers, not a fresh database capture.
Database length changes during capture produce incomplete outcome, without retry.
A changed physical media file is not automatically recaptured as a new trusted identity by the old changed-source latch.
currentChangedSourceCheck.proposalScope: Decision5 response policy now approved: report/exclude changed read and allow manual rescan, physical row/unaffected facts and approved fallbacks preserved. Exact detection mechanism, PMR DTM exclusion and header-opening rules are not changed by that approval.

currentCancelCloseCheck.head: c2cc89e9404fae5f84787c624f14e16d862d68bc
findings: Current Cancel button immediately shows Cancelling and emits the request.
Closing the progress sheet/Escape requests cooperative cancellation; this differs from quitting the app.
OldScanner cancelScan sets state and atomic flag, with no worker join.
BackgroundJob restart and shutdown join synchronously and can wait indefinitely after a warning.
OldScanner is a MainWindow-owned child and calls shutdown in its destructor; final application destruction can therefore wait on that path.
Normal scanning activity already prevents another ordinary scan before completion.
currentCancelCloseCheck.limits: Source-only review; no executed UI test, blocked-drive experiment or observed frequency/latency claim. Current Cancel is not claimed to block.
currentCancelCloseCheck.proposalScope: Bella scan cleanup/app closing only. Preserve partial results and existing file-operation/Bin Filter scope. No instant-safe-quit promise for blocked operating-system reads.

currentProgressWarningCheck.head: c2cc89e9404fae5f84787c624f14e16d862d68bc
findings: Progress emits per callback without a time throttle.
Warnings accumulate to50 log entries or an earlier phase/read flush.
Worker writes full supplied log messages before queued Console delivery.
Header read checkpoints use10000ms and reset on each logged source start; database starts are logged.
Console appends a combined batch string; its existing visible-history maximum is2000 blocks, distinct from disk logging.
currentProgressWarningCheck.limits: Read-only source check; no measured queue backlog or performance gain. Existing log persistence is behaviour, not an unlimited-history or filesystem-success guarantee.
